title: Tensor constructibility for admissible coefficients
statement: Let ell be prime and k a positive-characteristic field of characteristic different from ell. Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring satisfying IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ell Lambda. Let the schemes and morphisms be separated of finite type over k. For any K and M on X which are constant-model bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude, their specified relative derived tensor is constant-model bounded constructible. No Tor-amplitude conclusion is asserted here.

proof.text: Since $X$ is finite type over a field, it is Noetherian and qcqs (apply the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma; separatedness supplies quasi-separatedness). Unpack the seven alternatives in $h\Lambda$ and transport both factors along $e:\Lambda\cong\Lambda'$ to the indicated canonical coefficient by the coefficient-isomorphism lemma. The ring-isomorphism tensor comparison identifies the transported specified tensor with the tensor of the transported factors, so it suffices to prove constructibility at $\Lambda'$. Transport back (no Tor bound needed): restriction along $p_X^*e$ is an exact equivalence [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](4),(5), so it commutes with cohomology and boundedness; it commutes with restriction to strata and covers [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso] and sends a model $\Lambda'_U\otimes_{\Lambda'(*)}P$ to $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$, $P$ finitely presented via $e(*)$.

source.place: Coefficient normalization, original Lean proof paragraph 1.

proof.text: For finite $A$, every ideal is finite, so $A$ is Noetherian. The finite-Tor comparison descends both factors to bounded constructible etale complexes with ordered Tor intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$. The flat-constructible-model theorem gives representatives $P,Q$ in those intervals. Apply the new total-tensor lemma: it gives the bounded flat constructible total complex, its constructible cohomology, its K-flat derived identification and summed Tor interval. The monoidal comparison for $\nu_X^*$ identifies its pullback with the specified pro-etale tensor; the finite-Tor comparison places this pullback in $\Dctf$, hence in the required constant-model bounded constructible category.

source.place: Proof (1),(2), finite A; original proof step 1 and Lean paragraph 2.

proof.text: For $\mathcal O_E$ use clause (2) of integral-model operations. For $E$ and the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure use clause (1) of rational tensor closure. These assert closure of $\Dbc$ itself, so the input Tor hypotheses need no further identification of categories. The cases $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ are $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Proof (1),(2), integral and rational coefficients; original proof step 2.

proof.text: For the all-continuous algebraic closure use the new finite-cone generation theorem, with its exact constant-model convention and triangulated target. On two generators $a_!L,b_!M$, the new intersection comparison identifies their tensor with $c_!(r^*L\otimes s^*M)$ on $W=S\times_XT$. Its rank-product finite free local model and zero model off $W$ put it in that target. Derived tensor is exact in each variable: choose a K-flat representative and apply the tensor-triangulated lemma (and symmetry for the other variable). Induct first through a finite cone construction of the second factor for each first generator, then through that of the first factor. Shifts, zero and each triangle remain in the triangulated target. This proves this last coefficient case without identifying it with finite-subextension-valued sections. Step 1 finishes the original statement. All three new lemmas include the zero and empty cases.

source.place: Original Lean proof paragraph 3; lisse-generator argument of rational tensor closure, proof (1).

proof_origin.place: Finite flat models and integral/rational cases as in proof (1),(2); all-continuous case uses the original Lean docstring and the separate rational lisse-generator argument, without identifying the two algebraic-closure coefficients.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q60-a70c54543 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX: the re-split is faithful. I compared the base proof with the new one step by step. The old finite total-tensor calculation (common refinement, 094H, flat terms, 03RZ Serre closure, 06YQ K-flatness, summed Tor interval) is now the new node lem-sfb-finite-flat-constructible-total-tensor. The old all-continuous Q̄ℓ paragraph is now lem-sfb-continuous-qbar-constructible-generators (finite-cone generation equality plus triangulated target) and lem-sfb-locally-closed-generator-tensor-intersection (a_!L⊗b_!M ≅ c_!(r^*L⊗s^*M) on W=S×_X T, free of rank mn). The parent keeps the descent, the ν^* monoidal comparison, the integral and rational citations and the two-variable induction. The assembly is 2864 characters after my fix. The statement is byte-identical to live, and the item is not dropped or superseded. Source checks: the generator and intersection nodes follow sk-thm-sf-pf-field-tensor.proof.md (1) step for step, and the finite node follows sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images.proof.md (1),(2). There is no SGA. All three new nodes are true. C(S,Ω) with the ℓ-adic topology is strictly larger than the finite-subextension ring, so the existing generation and heart nodes (det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation, det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure, lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-serre) and IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient do not cover it, and the generator node is not a duplicate. Its truth rests on the field scalar ring (lisse = finite free), on lisse modules being representations of π1^proet (BS 7.4.7), and on extensions splitting on w-contractible covers. The intersection node uses the open/closed projection formulas plus base change and holds for any condensed Λ. None of the new nodes restates the item. Step 3 correctly drops the old unsupported claim that Step 1 identifies these categories with Dctf. Repaired fault (C-type missing citation): step 1 transported the tensor back with lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible, whose statement covers only Dctf, but the tensor is known only to lie in Dbc (the item asserts no Tor bound). I added the justification: restriction along p_X^*e is an exact equivalence by sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars (4),(5), it commutes with pullback to strata and covers by def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso, and it carries finite constant models to finite constant models through e(*). I updated uses, proof_deps and tool_uses to match. Corrected file: fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-admissible-tensor-constructibility.json. Maintainer note: blueprint.from.node is null on the new nodes because the item's created.item names a Lean module, which breaks the ancestry chain.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
